Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the draft Order Form (attached). We have one unusual requirement coming from our finance team related to a legacy entitlement that sits on a different GreenGrid legal entity. Before we start redlining, a couple quick asks:

- Which legal entity will Redwood invoice in the current draft? The header shows "GreenGrid Analytics, Inc." but our legacy entitlement should be billed to "GreenGrid Solutions, LLC".
- If we route that portion of fees to Solutions, will Redwood accept an entity-level carveout in the order form so that invoicing and tax responsibilities follow Solutions?
- Our AP also needs to confirm whether Redwood expects us to withhold any VAT/withholding tax at source for that entity — we haven’t applied withholding historically, but the auditors want this documented.

I've attached the draft and a copy of the Solutions tax cert. Can we get confirmation on whether Redwood can: (1) route invoices to a different remit-to entity for legacy entitlements, and (2) include clear language about tax withholding / withholding liability in the order form (or MSA) so our tax team can approve?

Would prefer a short call if anything is unclear — Emily

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear note and for sending the tax cert.

Short answers up front: yes, we can route invoices to a different remit-to entity for a carveout of the order, and we can add explicit tax-withholding language — but we need to agree the exact clause and confirm whether Redwood or GreenGrid carries withholding responsibility (and how that interacts with the invoicing entity).

What I propose:
- Redwood will add an "Entity carveout" section to the Order Form that ties a line-item group (legacy entitlement SKU list) to GreenGrid Solutions, LLC as the invoice recipient.
- The Order Form will include a tax appendix: standard language that says the customer is responsible for any taxes, including withholding taxes, unless a specific written agreement (tax certificate or local ruling) requires otherwise.
- For this carveout, if GreenGrid requests Redwood to gross-up amounts to account for withholding, we need to capture that as an amendment (and it will impact pricing).

Lauren from Finance is looped in to confirm billing and PO flow; Ben/Vivek are on the thread for commercial approvals.

If that direction works, I can have legal draft the two short clauses for review by EOD today and share an updated Order Form (v3). If you prefer a call, we can do a 20-min sync tomorrow morning.

Kimberly / team — thanks, Emily, for the detail. Drafting notes below (high level). I'll prepare language for the Order Form + an MSA side-note.

- Invoice routing carveout: a new paragraph in the Order Form that reads (draft):
  "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Master Services Agreement, the fees attributable to the products and services listed in Appendix A (\"Legacy Entitlements\") shall be invoiced to and payable by GreenGrid Solutions, LLC (\"Invoice Recipient\"). Redwood shall deliver invoices and billing notices to the Invoice Recipient at the address set forth in Appendix A. All other fees shall remain payable by the Customer entity identified in the Order Form header."

- Tax / withholding: propose the following short clause:
  "Taxes; Withholding. Except for taxes based on Redwood's net income, Customer shall be responsible for all applicable taxes, duties, and withholding taxes arising from Customer's use of the Services. If Customer is required by law to withhold any amounts from payments to Redwood, Customer shall: (a) provide Redwood with written notice and supporting documentation prior to withholding; (b) use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize withholding; and (c) if requested by Redwood, provide certified tax documentation evidencing the withholding. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, prices in the Order Form do not include any withholding tax; if withholding applies, Customer shall either gross-up the payment so that Redwood receives the full amount invoiced or provide Redwood with official evidence that the withholding was made and paid to the relevant authority."
- Practical ask for GreenGrid: please confirm whether Solutions will be providing the PO, and whether Solutions will ask Redwood to gross-up. If they will not gross-up, we need a PO + tax evidence to avoid disputes on remittance amounts.

I will attach a tracked-change Order Form (v3) with the carveout and tax appendix for review this afternoon.

Looping in a commercial point: if Solutions will be the invoice recipient only for a subset of SKUs, we should make sure the pricing schedule shows which line items are carved out and whether minimum commitment bands still apply pro-rata. Two commercial options to consider:

1) Keep total ACV intact and split invoicing entity only for collection and tax purposes (ACV and min-commit still evaluated at the customer level).
2) Treat the carved-out legacy entitlement as a distinct bill-to/account with its own min-commit and invoicing cadence (simpler for accounting on GG side but may change discounts).

My recommendation: prefer option 1 if GreenGrid wants to keep overall discounting intact; option 2 only if Solutions insists on independent netterms / PO flow. We'll need finance to confirm how option 2 would affect revenue recognition — Lauren, can you weigh in?

Ben Carter
VP, Sales — US
